problem: A configured client already connected to endpoint A saved wizard changes for B but retained its live API/agent on A, especially with AutoConnect=false.

correction.reconnect: After Apply, an existing connection is explicitly rebound even if automatic startup connection is disabled. An unconnected manual profile remains manual.
correction.admission: Configuration lease covers dialog/application and releases before ConnectAsync obtains its own lease. No foreground LLM turn may overlap.
correction.surface: Agent memory/provider reference, session ID, messages/sources, staged composer, old notices and background trackers are cleared before a connection attempt and again on failure. Failed target never leaves an old agent usable.
correction.sessionHint: A prior session hint is reused only for an initial connection or an unchanged endpoint/key/user context. Changed contexts load fresh server history.
correction.background: Each advanced/direct tracker owns an API snapshot retaining its endpoint and identity. Late persistence remains on that owner endpoint. UI updates require matching active connection. Old terminal owners cannot remove a newer tracker with the same job ID.
correction.credentials: Admin session is cleared before configuring the foreground target. Snapshot comparison includes backend URL, API key and user identity without exposing them.
correction.localModel: Foreground turn gate prevents overlapping generation while provider and agent are replaced. The shared local transport remains configured through the existing factory; no local process is force-stopped by reconfiguration.
correction.errors: Known HTTP401/403, other HTTP failures and TLS errors are localized without copying raw English exception text. Full details remain diagnostic logs.

scope: Real ApiClient requests through deterministic transport prove snapshots retain old host/key after foreground reconfiguration
Late old-owner PATCH stays on old host after failed new-target GET
Identity changes on same endpoint do not match old owners
Compiled handlers/trackers use policy, reset and owned snapshots
Existing W29/W30 and advanced transport/handoff contracts

architecture.change: Pure network error classification extracted from MainWindow into its own service before localized HTTP handling was added. No ceiling raised.

limitations: Snapshot APIs retain their configuration because their owners never retarget them; ApiClient itself remains a configurable type.
BackendUrlPicker still selects the fastest reachable configured candidate. A test asserting a particular new URL must account for any configured alternatives.
Connection clearing intentionally prevents retaining an old endpoint's visible conversation/composer as usable context after Apply; failed rebind exposes a disconnected error state.

These tests do not execute the real UI. Root must rebuild production after closing the current client, then verify Apply changes the next actual request target, same-endpoint credential changes, failed rebind, and localized authentication recovery.
